items.title: Louis Armstrong Interview, 1960-08-02
items.q: Yes, Danny Kay and all of them. Just during the time we made five pennants, and he'd be reloading the camera.

ctx.x: You've worked with a lot of good people, Louie, in your time. Outside of musicians, who are some of the top people you think? I mean, you've worked with Danny Kay, of course.

Yes, Danny Kay and all of them. Just during the time we made five pennants, and he'd be reloading the camera. I'm in his office looking at the World Series ballgame. And then they'd say, all on. Oh, Wenderson, you know Gustav Mahler? Oh, the rock monitor, just that easy. We don't even bother about it. One more time. One more time. See? And I look at them, and they're so great. They run their script down and put it in the pocket and talk about something else. Well, I'm going to do that, too. And Dick Powell was…

You were talking earlier about the orchestras in the old days and the playing for the funerals and the impromptu stuff on the street corner. Is that being done at all anymore? Who's doing it? Are these names? The younger generation. Are we going to hear from them?
